evals.prompt: With php-patterns loaded, implement a small behaviour change in a PHP class in a target repo (e.g. add a typed method that validates input and can fail).
evals.expected_output: A scoped change with declare(strict_types=1), full type declarations, strict comparisons, PSR-12 style, plus PHPUnit tests covering the behaviour with a boundary and an exception case; PHPStan/Psalm and the formatter clean using the repo's own composer scripts.
assertions: declare(strict_types=1) is present and params/returns/properties are type-declared
Strict comparison (===) is used, not loose ==
PHPUnit tests cover the happy path plus a boundary and an exception case
No obvious static-analysis errors (PHPStan/Psalm-level) on inspection and PSR-12 formatting is applied
No existing test is weakened, skipped, or deleted

evals.prompt: With php-patterns loaded, add code that runs a database query using a user-supplied value.
evals.expected_output: A prepared statement with bound parameters (never string-built SQL), the input validated at the boundary, and deterministic tests; no secret logged.
assertions: The query uses a prepared statement with bound parameters (no string-concatenated SQL)
User input (superglobals/external) is validated at the trust boundary
Tests are deterministic (no real network/DB; the boundary is stubbed)
No secret or credential is logged

component.purpose: The PHP conventions and toolchain the software-engineer/qa-engineer (and the code-review lint aspect) apply when the detected stack is PHP; a lean, loaded-on-demand knowledge pack exercised through the software-engineer's Tier-2.
